# jochwacht-sbom 0.15.0 — the condition on the edge counts too

`uv.lock` writes an environment condition in two places: on the package
entry (`resolution-markers`, read since 0.14.0) and on the dependency edge
itself:

```toml
dependencies = [{ name = "colorama", marker = "sys_platform == 'win32'" }]
```

0.14.0 read only the first kind and said so. This release reads both.

Measured on the same real lockfile as before, target
`python=3.10;platform=linux;arch=aarch64,x86_64`: three more resolutions are
not shipped — `colorama` (win32 only), `setuptools` (3.12 and up only) and
`opencv-python` (replaced by the headless build through an
`override-dependencies` entry, which uv writes as `sys_platform == '_'`).
Nine of 120 components in total, and the count stays at 120: nothing is
deleted.

## Why this needed a graph

The rule is the difference of **two** traversals: reachable when conditions
are ignored, not reachable when they are honoured. Plain reachability would
also have caught every development dependency — those are unreachable from
the production roots for an entirely different reason, and calling them "not
shipped into your target environment" would be a false statement about your
project.

A package that drops out because its *parent* is not shipped is told exactly
that, and not "a condition that is false" — the first version of this change
printed the latter next to a condition that was true.

## Safety

- No workspace members in the lockfile means no roots and therefore no
  reachability statement: then nothing happens. Without that guard a plain
  lockfile would have collapsed the whole bill to "not shipped".
- An edge condition that cannot be decided counts as satisfiable.
- `Foo_Bar` and `foo-bar` are one project (PEP 503). Treating them as two
  nodes excluded a package that was reachable.
- Without `--target-env` the graph is not even built and the output is
  unchanged.

## The limit that is not in the code

`--target-env` has to be the environment you really ship. Nothing checks it
against `requires-python`: declare 3.10 while shipping 3.12 and the
`setuptools` exclusion above becomes a false statement about your product.
The declaration decides what you are liable for — check it, do not guess it.
